summary.motive: Make the playside end choose between the dive and the keep, then punish any third defender who joins with the pitch phase.
summary.whyItWorks: The veer mesh makes the end's crash feel mandatory, and once he commits the geometry guarantees either a free keep lane or an untouched pitch around displaced force.
summary.failureMode: The end squeezes and spilles simultaneously while the force corner stays flat-footed, collapsing all three phases into one gap.

beats.title: 1. Ride and Read the End
beats.text: The quarterback seats the ball on B's hip riding the veer mesh while staring at the playside end — the one defender left unblocked on the entire play.

beats.title: 2. The End Crashes Down
beats.text: The end shoots inside across B's face to make the dive tackle. By taking the dive he hands the quarterback a free pull and an empty C-gap.

beats.title: 3. The Pitch Relationship
beats.text: The keep bends off the down-blocked 3-tech while A mirrors from the perimeter. Their spacing forces every second-level defender to declare before the ball moves.

beats.title: 4. Pitch and Perimeter Finish
beats.text: When the force corner triggers upfield, the pitch goes out. A takes it around the kick-out with the safety and free safety both committed inside.

relations.tell: The dive aims at the B-gap behind the down-blocked tackle and the read is the wide end — midline reads interior and dives at the guard-center seam.
